IF YOU WANT TO CRACK CODING INTERVIEWS, STOP PRACTICING RANDOMLY.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 PATTERNS INSTEAD: 1/5

Two pointers turn O(n^2) into O(n).

Sorted array, pair sum, container with water. Move ends inward instead of nesting loops. 2/5

Sliding window owns substring problems.

Longest, shortest, best. Grow the right edge, shrink the left when invalid. One pass. 3/5

BFS and DFS are the same skill.

Grids, islands, trees, graphs. Queue for shortest path, stack for exhaustive search. Learn both once. 4/5

IF YOU WANT TO BECOME A TOP 1% PROBLEM SOLVER, STOP SKIPPING THE BASICS.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 HABITS: 1/5

Always clarify before coding.

Inputs, edge cases, constraints. Five minutes of questions saves thirty minutes of rewrites. 2/5

Brute force first, on purpose.

Write the ugly O(n^2), then ask what repeats. The optimal solution hides inside the naive one. 3/5

Time yourself, then review.

45 minutes per problem max. The learning happens in the 15 minutes after, studying the pattern you missed. 4/5

IF YOU WANT TO MASTER DYNAMIC PROGRAMMING, STOP FEARING IT.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 STEPS: 1/5

Ask one question: does the answer build from smaller answers?

If yes, it's DP. If no, stop forcing it. 2/5

Define the state in one sentence.

dp[i] means the best answer for the first i items. Vague state, wrong answer. 3/5

Write the recurrence before any code.

How does dp[i] use dp[i-1]? One line of math beats fifty lines of guessing. 4/5
